summary: The payment-service outage is a symptom, not the fault. The shared ledger-db Postgres filled to 100% disk, driven by an inactive replication slot ('analytics_cdc') retaining tens of GB of WAL. Disk climbed steadily 89%->100% between 13:00 and 14:50; Postgres then failed with 'No space left on device' / 'could not extend file'. All write-path clients of ledger-db broke at ~15:00 - payment-service ("ledger write failed") AND order-service ("INSERT INTO orders failed"), the latter with no deployment of its own. This rules out the v6.0.0 deploy (rolled back 15:12 without recovery; disk was already ~98% before the 14:46 deploy) and points to resource_exhaustion originating in ledger-db. The v6.0.0 'new ledger entry type' is coincidental; payment-service's write-heavy path made it the loudest victim.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db disk full from inactive replication slot retaining WAL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: On the shared ledger-db Postgres, the replication slot 'analytics_cdc' went inactive and retained tens of GB of WAL, steadily consuming disk from ~89% up to 100% by ~14:50. Once full, Postgres could no longer write WAL or extend files, so all write-path clients of ledger-db (payment-service, order-service) failed with 'No space left on device'. The fault originates in ledger-db/infrastructure, not in any service code.

causal_chain.claim: analytics_cdc replication slot inactive -> WAL retained (F2, F13)
retained WAL -> disk fills 89%->100% by 14:50 (F1, F3)
disk 100% -> Postgres PANIC / cannot extend file (F4)
shared ledger-db write failures -> payment-service AND order-service 5xx at ~15:00 (F5, F8)
errors persist after rollback because fault is not in the deploy (F9)

assumptions: The 'analytics_cdc' slot retention is the dominant cause of the disk growth vs. ordinary data growth (log shows repeated large WAL retention, but total disk budget unknown)
No concurrent capacity/disk resize event explains the fill

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow / new ledger entry type caused failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v6.0.0 release's new MANDATE_HOLD ledger flow produced excessive writes or an error that broke ledger writes, causing payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Disk was already ~98% before the 14:46 deploy and 100% by 14:50; an undeployed sibling service (order-service) failed simultaneously with the identical 'No space left on device' error; and errors continued at ~60% after the 15:12 rollback. A code rollback did not restore service.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Credential/TLS or clock issue on payment-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A deprecated TLS cipher / clock drift noticed in logs caused the outage.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: TLS cipher and clock-drift warnings are single, sparse, and unrelated to the 'No space left on device' errors that dominate both payment-service and ledger-db logs.

facts.statement: ledger-db disk_used_pct reached 100% by ~14:50 and stayed at 100% through 16:50.
ledger-db replication slot 'analytics_cdc' was inactive and retaining up to ~92 GB of WAL starting before the incident.
ledger-db logged disk usage warnings 90% -> 98% before failing.
ledger-db threw PANIC 'No space left on device' and 'could not extend file' errors from 15:01.
payment-service threw 354 'ledger write failed: ...No space left on device' errors from 15:00:26.
payment-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~61% at 15:00, not at the 14:46 deploy.
The only change was payment-service v6.0.0 (deployed 14:46, rolled back 15:12); no config/flag changes.
order-service, not deployed, began 'No space left on device' failures at 15:00:42 and error_rate jumped to ~48%, the same ledger-db symptom.
payment-service errors persisted at ~60% after the 15:12 rollback.
portfolio-service (also a ledger-db client) was unaffected at ~0.2%.
ledger-db is a shared Postgres used by order-, portfolio-, payment-, and settlement-service.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms grew monotonically (2340ms -> 5213ms), consistent with retained WAL on a slot.
Prior incident HIST-114 had the identical root cause (inactive replication slot retaining WAL filling disk).

assumptions: The repeated 'analytics_cdc inactive, retaining N MB of WAL' messages are caused by a genuinely abandoned CDC consumer rather than a transient hiccup that self-resolved.
Metric values are per the shared service scope; disk_used_pct reflects the ledger-db data volume that payments and orders write to.

timeline.event: ledger-db begins warning that slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive and retaining WAL; disk ~89%.
payment-service begins 'ledger write failed: No space left on device'.
order-service begins 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device'.
ledger-db PANIC writing WAL: No space left on device.
payment-service v6.0.0 rolled back; errors continue.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately free disk on ledger-db: drop the inactive 'analytics_cdc' replication slot (after confirming it is unused) to release retained WAL, or add disk capacity as a stopgap.
recommended_actions.rationale: The disk is pinned at 100% and Postgres PANICs on WAL writes; releasing retained WAL is the direct fix (matches HIST-114 resolution).

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating this as a payment-service deploy problem - the v6.0.0 rollback did not recover service; keep the rollback decision under review but focus on ledger-db.
recommended_actions.rationale: Errors persisted after 15:12 rollback and an undeployed service failed identically.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on replication-slot lag/retained WAL size and on ledger-db disk >85%.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both this and HIST-114 were silent disk fills from a slot; an early alert would have caught it hours earlier.

recommended_actions.action: Audit all replication slots (especially 'analytics_cdc') for ownership/monitoring and add auto-drop or watchdog policy for inactive slots.
recommended_actions.rationale: Recurring class of failure; needs governance.

data_gaps: Total disk size/absolute free bytes on ledger-db not available (only disk_used_pct), so the exact contribution of WAL retention vs. ordinary data growth cannot be quantified.
No ledger-db node/infra event log to confirm whether any disk resize or maintenance occurred.
bank-partner-api has no telemetry; its state during the incident is unknown (no evidence it was involved, but unverified).

findings.statement: ledger-db disk usage climbed steadily from ~89% at 13:00 to 100% by 14:50 and stayed pinned at 100% through 16:50.
ledger-db logs repeatedly report the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining large amounts of WAL (up to ~92 GB) starting well before the incident.

refs.quote: replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 92599 MB of WAL

findings.statement: ledger-db emitted disk-space warnings rising 90% -> 98% in the hours before the failure.
ledger-db threw PANIC 'No space left on device' writing WAL and 'could not extend file' errors starting 15:01.

refs.quote: PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478": No space left on device

findings.statement: payment-service logged 354 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' errors starting 15:00:26.

refs.quote: ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device (payment e3489438)

findings.statement: payment-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% (through 14:50) to ~61% at 15:00 and remained ~60-64% through 16:50, i.e. the rise occurred at the disk-full onset, not at the 14:46 deploy.
The only deployment in the window was payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46, rolled back at 15:12; it is the sole code change and there were zero config/flag changes.

order-service, a service NOT deployed in this window and also a client of ledger-db, began failing at 15:00:42 with 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' and its error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~48% at 15:00.

refs.quote: INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device orderId=8ab6dc3a

findings.statement: Error rate for payment-service remained ~60% after the 15:12 rollback, through the last data point 16:50.
portfolio-service (also a ledger-db client) error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout, indicating its path was read-only/unaffected.
ledger-db is a shared Postgres datastore used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms rose monotonically across the window (2340ms -> 5213ms), consistent with a stuck/retained WAL on a replication slot.
A prior incident HIST-114 (2025-04-18) had the same root cause: 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', category resource_exhaustion on ledger-db.

refs.quote: Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled
